# replayr

[![Lifecycle:
experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)

`replayr` imports emulator recordings into R. It reads the buttons,
keys, analogue sticks, pointer movement, touch, and motion-sensor values
recorded during play, together with their timing and emulator metadata.

![Gamepads, motion controllers, keyboards, mice, touchscreens, light
guns, arcade controls, keypads, and
dials](reference/figures/universal_buttons_layout.svg)

Gamepads, motion controllers, keyboards, mice, touchscreens, light guns,
arcade controls, keypads, and dials

## Getting started

Install from a source checkout:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_local("path/to/replayr")
```

Read a recording and extract one controller:

``` r

library(replayr)

path <- system.file("extdata", "sample.fm2", package = "replayr")
movie <- read_movie(path)
input <- player(movie, 1L)

n_frames(movie)
press_counts(movie)
button_layout(movie)
```

`input` is a logical matrix: rows are observations, columns are
controls, and `TRUE` means active.
[`button_layout()`](reference/button_layout.md) identifies each column.
For another recording, pass its path to
[`read_movie()`](reference/read_movie.md); the file extension selects
the reader. [`movie_members()`](reference/movie_members.md) lists
recordings inside a ZIP download, and `read_movie(path, member = ...)`
selects one of them.

## Controllers and control identities

Each S3 object contains digital inputs, numeric channels, commands, and
metadata. A `replayr_movie` stores its digital input in an array indexed
by observation, controller, and control. Event-based formats retain the
key and device fields present in the events; fixed gamepad layouts
include unused buttons as well as pressed ones.

Columns are compact within each recording. Stable IDs and keys identify
controls across layouts: a stick click, a direction derived from that
stick, and an N64 C-button each have their own identity.
`button_layout(movie)` gives the column-to-control mapping;
[`button_layout()`](reference/button_layout.md) lists the shared
registry. Keyboard identities retain the source convention, such as X
KeySyms or Windows virtual keys.

``` r

aligned <- align_buttons(list(movie1, movie2))
```

The aligned matrices have matching columns, with absent controls filled
by `FALSE`. Comparing game actions also requires a mapping from controls
to their in-game meanings, such as Jump or Attack.

## Analogue and positional input

[`analog_channels()`](reference/analog_channels.md) returns recorded
numeric values. By default, `analog = "raw"` leaves stick coordinates in
this form. Four options add directions or angles: `cardinal4`,
`cardinal8`, `angle`, and `angle+magnitude`. Settings can be chosen
independently for each stick:

``` r

path <- system.file("extdata", "sample.dtm", package = "replayr")
movie <- read_movie(path,
  analog = c(left = "angle+magnitude", right = "cardinal8"))
head(analog_channels(movie))
head(stick_channels(movie))
```

Cardinal modes add logical direction columns. Angles increase
counterclockwise from right: 0 degrees right, 90 up, 180 left, and 270
down. `deadzone` sets the radial threshold for an active direction.
Magnitude measures displacement after applying the controller’s centre
and scale; diagonal values can exceed one. The original coordinates
remain available in every mode.

Mouse movement, light-gun aim, touch coordinates, dials, and motion
sensors also appear in
[`analog_channels()`](reference/analog_channels.md), with names and
units determined by the recording format. Wii input can include
accelerometer values, infrared points, and MotionPlus readings. Sensor
calibration is needed to convert these counts to physical units. The
[introduction](vignettes/replayr.Rmd) demonstrates mouse dragging and
Wii motion with original examples included in the package.

For BK2 recordings, [`system_channels()`](reference/system_channels.md)
returns cabinet and emulator controls, such as coins, reset, disk
selection, and input timing.

## Timing and multiple controllers

Rows may represent video frames, controller polls, or timestamped
events. [`n_frames()`](reference/n_frames.md) counts imported
observations. The reader documentation describes the observation unit
and any timing information stored in the file. LSMV also records input
changes within video frames; `movie$subframes` identifies each
observation’s frame and position.

M64 and DTM can contain multiple controllers without identifying the
source port of each poll. These recordings return a
`replayr_poll_stream`:

``` r

path <- system.file("extdata", "paper", "unassigned.dtm", package = "replayr")
stream <- read_dtm(path)
polls(stream)
```

The polls retain their source order. A `controller_order` established
from the emulator can assign them to players. Wii and 3DS formats also
distinguish reports from different devices; their observation flags
identify which input fields each report supplies. See
[`?read_dtm`](reference/read_dtm.md) and
[`?read_ctm`](reference/read_ctm.md) for these fields.

## Formats and platforms

The package reads 34 format families, with HGM as an alias for Hourglass
WTF. The [compatibility catalogue](COMPATIBILITY.md) describes their
versions, controller variants, and platform coverage.

| Recording family | Emulator or recorder | Systems represented |
|----|----|----|
| FM2, FM3, FCM, FMV | FCEUX, FCEU, Famtasia | NES, Famicom Disk System |
| BK2, BKM, TAS, TASPROJ | BizHawk | Consoles, handhelds, arcade machines, and home computers |
| GBMV | GBAHawk | Game Boy Advance |
| LSMV, SMV, ZMV | lsnes, Snes9x, enhanced ZSNES | SNES, Game Boy, Super Game Boy |
| GMV | Gens | Mega Drive, Sega CD, 32X |
| MMV | Dega | Master System, Game Gear |
| VBM | VBA | Game Boy, Game Boy Color, Game Boy Advance |
| M64, GZM | Mupen64, GZ | Nintendo 64 |
| DSM | DeSmuME | Nintendo DS |
| CTM | Citra | Nintendo 3DS |
| PXM, PJM | PCSX-rr, PSXjin | PlayStation |
| DTM | Dolphin | GameCube, Wii |
| MC2 | PCEjin, VBjin | PC Engine, Virtual Boy |
| MCM | Mednafen-rr | PC Engine, PC-FX, Lynx, WonderSwan, Neo Geo Pocket, NES, Master System |
| YMV | Yabause-rr | Saturn |
| MAR | MAME-rr | Arcade games with known or supplied port schemas |
| FBM | FinalBurn Alpha | Arcade games with an explicit driver input layout |
| DFT | Dustmod | *Dustforce* input scripts and their dependencies |
| LMP | Doom, Boom | Doom 1.9 and Boom demo versions 200–202 |
| LTM | libTAS | Linux applications, including emulated systems |
| WTF, HGM | Hourglass | Windows applications |
| JRSR | JPC-rr | DOS PC |
| OMR | openMSX | MSX, Spectravideo SVI-318/328 |
| CTAS | CoffeeTools | *UFO 50* |

The supported recording formats cover the following platforms. Some
desktop and browser entries use input recorded by a host application
through libTAS or Hourglass; the catalogue identifies those
combinations.

| Family | Platforms |
|----|----|
| Nintendo | Nintendo Entertainment System / Famicom; Famicom Disk System; Super Nintendo / Super Famicom; Satellaview; Game Boy; Game Boy Color; Game Boy Advance; Super Game Boy; Nintendo 64; Nintendo 64DD; Nintendo DS; Nintendo DSi; Nintendo 3DS; Nintendo GameCube; Wii; Virtual Boy. |
| Sega | Sega Genesis / Mega Drive; Sega CD / Mega-CD; Sega 32X; Sega Master System; Game Gear; Sega SG-1000; Sega Saturn. |
| Atari | Atari 2600; Atari 7800; Atari Jaguar; Atari Jaguar CD; Atari Lynx. |
| NEC | PC Engine / TurboGrafx-16; PC Engine CD / TurboGrafx-CD; SuperGrafx; PC-FX; NEC PC-98. |
| Other consoles | 3DO; CD-i; Fairchild Channel F; ColecoVision; Intellivision; Neo Geo Pocket; Odyssey 2 / Videopac; Sony PlayStation; WonderSwan; Uzebox; Vectrex. |
| Home computers and calculators | Amiga; Apple II; Commodore 64; MSX Home Computer System; Spectravideo SVI-318/328; ZX Spectrum; Texas Instruments TI-83 Series. |
| Arcade and application platforms | Arcade; IBM PC DOS; IBM PC compatible; Mac OS / macOS; Android; Java 2 Platform, Micro Edition (J2ME); Adobe Flash; PICO-8; TIC-80; Web. |

Arcade FBM recordings require a `game` identifier or `input_schema`,
since their fields follow the game driver’s order. Decoding legacy Wii
extension controls requires the extension type and, when encrypted, its
key. Reader help pages describe the arguments needed for each variant.

## Large recordings

For BK2 logs that are too large to hold in memory, use a callback on
successive chunks:

``` r

counts <- read_bk2_chunks("long-recording.bk2", press_counts)
Reduce(`+`, counts)
```

The input log is checked and extracted once. Temporary disk space must
hold the expanded log; the callback determines how much output is
retained. [`read_bk2()`](reference/read_bk2.md) and
[`read_lsmv()`](reference/read_lsmv.md) limit full imports to 256 MiB of
expanded input by default. `max_input_bytes` can raise this limit when
memory permits.

## Tests and examples

The package includes original artificial recordings and their
generators. They exercise individual controls, movement patterns, device
combinations, and malformed input. Run the tests with
`devtools::test("path/to/replayr")`. Optional external tests use
separately obtained TASVideos recordings through `REPLAYR_FIXTURE_DIR`.

documentation and emulator source references are listed in

## Inspect observations and controllers

- [`replayr_movie`](replayr_movie.md) :

  The `replayr_movie` S3 class

- [`replayr_poll_stream`](replayr_poll_stream.md) : Ordered controller
  and device polls

- [`polls()`](polls.md) : Extract an unassigned controller-poll stream

- [`n_frames()`](n_frames.md) : Number of observations in an imported
  recording

- [`n_players()`](n_players.md) : Number of assigned input streams

- [`n_buttons()`](n_buttons.md) : Number of compact controller columns

- [`player()`](player.md) : Button states for one controller

- [`press_counts()`](press_counts.md) : Held-observation counts per
  control

- [`button_layout()`](button_layout.md) : Stable controller identities
  and compact movie columns

- [`align_buttons()`](align_buttons.md) : Align compact controller
  matrices by stable button identity

- [`analog_channels()`](analog_channels.md) : Numeric analogue channels
  for one player

- [`stick_channels()`](stick_channels.md) : Selected stick directions,
  angles and magnitudes

- [`system_channels()`](system_channels.md) : Global emulator and
  cabinet controls
